parts.title: Word List
parts.content:
Detailed Meanings

😎
accelerate[ækseləreit]v.
To accelerate means to increase in speed.
→ When he stepped on the gas pedal, the motorcycle accelerated.
😎
anew[ənu:]adv.
If you do something anew, you do it again and in a different way.
→ Though he had failed his driving test, he decided to try it anew.
😎
defect[difekt]n.
A defect is a part of something that is wrong or missing.
→ All these bottles have a defect and must be sent back to the warehouse.
😎
dreary[driəri]adj.
If something is dreary, then it is dull, dark, and lifeless.
→ After the fire, this section of forest is rather dreary.
😎
duplicate[dju:pləkeit]v.
To duplicate something means to copy it.
→ She duplicated her friend’s movements like she was in front of a mirror.
😎
electromagnetic[ilektroumægnetik]adj.
If something is electromagnetic, it is related to electricity and magnetic fields.
→ Different colors of light come from different levels of electromagnetic energy.
😎
electron[ilektrɔn]n.
An electron is a particle in all atoms that has a negative electric charge.
→ The number of electrons in an atom determines the substance the atoms make.
😎
glide[glaid]v.
To glide means to fly on extended wings with little or no effort.
→ When the wind is blowing, birds can glide easily through the sky.
😎
ingenious[indʒi:njəs]adj.
If someone is ingenious, then they are very smart.
→ Charles was the only person ingenious enough to repair the plane’s engines.
😎
innovation[inouveiʃən]n.
An innovation is a product or an idea that is new or very original.
→ Mrs. Johnson made a great innovation to the company’s business plan.
😎
innovative[inouveitiv]adj.
If something or someone is innovative, they can think in creative ways.
→ Since Peter was so innovative, he was chosen to lead the science team.
😎
launch[lɔ:ntʃ]v.
To launch something means to make it go into motion.
→ The boat launched from the dock and floated down the river.
😎
meteorological[mi:tiərəlɔdʒikəl]adj.
If something is meteorological, it is concerned with the science of weather.
→ The thunderstorm was so large that it became a great meteorological event.
😎
meteorology[mi:tiərɔlədʒi]n.
Meteorology is the science that studies the weather.
→ In order to understand the weather, you have to study meteorology.
😎
penetrate[penətreit]v.
To penetrate something means to enter into it.
→ The knife easily penetrated the surface of the orange.
😎
propulsion[prəpʌlʃən]n.
Propulsion is the force that moves something forward.
→ The propulsion lifted the rocket into the sky.
😎
simulate[simjəleit]v.
To simulate something means to copy its actions or characteristics.
→ The French language teacher could simulate the accent of a French citizen.
😎
spur[spə:r]v.
To spur someone means to urge them into action.
→ The coach’s speech spurred her team into playing the best game of their lives.
😎
stimulate[stimjəleit]v.
To stimulate something means to cause or to increase activity in it.
→ Doctors sometimes use electric shock to stimulate a patient’s heartbeat.
😎
tenacious[təneiʃəs]adj.
If someone is tenacious, then they do not easily give up.
→ I’m sure that he’ll finish that difficult sale. He is very tenacious.

sections.title: Exercise 1: Choose the one that is similar in meaning to the given word.

questions.content: 1. defect
questions.explanation: defect (n): a part of something that is wrong or missing. Similar to broken.

questions.content: 2. innovation
questions.explanation: innovation (n): a product or an idea that is new or very original. Similar to original.

questions.content: 3. accelerate
questions.explanation: accelerate (v): to increase in speed. Similar to speed up.

questions.content: 4. meteorological
questions.explanation: meteorological (adj): concerned with the science of weather. Similar to weather.

questions.content: 5. dreary
questions.explanation: dreary (adj): dull, dark, and lifeless. Similar to dull.

sections.title: Exercise 2: Write a word that is similar in meaning to the underlined part.

questions.content: 1. You can hear because sound causes activity in the tiny hairs on the inside of your ear.
questions.explanation: stimulates means to cause or to increase activity in.

questions.content: 2. Some worms are small enough to enter into the skin without being detected.
questions.explanation: penetrate means to enter into it.

questions.content: 3. She tried to copy the way her best friend dressed.
questions.explanation: duplicate means to copy it.

questions.content: 4. The teacher offered the kids candy in order to urge them into finishing their homework.
questions.explanation: spur means to urge them into action.

questions.content: 5. In science class, we learned about the particles in atoms that have a negative electric charge.
questions.explanation: electron is a particle in all atoms that has a negative electric charge.

questions.content: 6. Every time the children’s fort fell down, they built it again and better.
questions.explanation: anew means again and in a different way.

questions.content: 7. She took classes in the science that studies the weather and became a weatherperson.
questions.explanation: meteorology is the science that studies the weather.

questions.content: 8. The small airplane flew without any effort through the sky.
questions.explanation: glided means flew on extended wings with little or no effort.

questions.content: 9. A rocket requires a lot of fuel in order to start it into the sky.
questions.explanation: launch means to make it go into motion.

questions.content: 10. Amanda is quite an intelligent girl for her young age.
questions.explanation: ingenious means very smart.

sections.title: Exercise 3: Write C if the italicized word is used correctly. Write I if the word is used incorrectly.

questions.content: 1. Just when you thought you’d caught up to Brian, he’d accelerate and quickly get away.
questions.explanation: accelerate means to increase in speed.

questions.content: 2. The orchestra made a very tenacious sound, and many in the audience decided to leave.
questions.explanation: tenacious means not giving up easily, not a sound.

questions.content: 3. Dan had duplicated the sculpture exactly. It now looked nothing like the original one.
questions.explanation: duplicated means copied exactly, so it would look like the original.

questions.content: 4. Lions are dangerous hunters. They can glide through the air to capture their prey.
questions.explanation: lions do not glide (fly on wings).

questions.content: 5. They had a picnic in the park and launched on small sandwiches and grapes.
questions.explanation: launched means to put into motion, not eaten.

questions.content: 6. We made a small toy train that stimulated how real trains worked 100 years ago.
questions.explanation: should be simulated, not stimulated.

questions.content: 7. Cellular phones are one of the most popular innovations in the world today.
questions.explanation: innovation is a new product or idea.

questions.content: 8. The knight’s sword could not penetrate his opponent’s armor.
questions.explanation: penetrate means to enter into.

questions.content: 9. The thought of his warm bed spurred the traveler on through the cold night.
questions.explanation: spurred means urged into action.

questions.content: 10. We didn’t mind that our paintings got ruined. It was fun to start them anew.
questions.explanation: anew means again.

questions.content: 11. Satellites are very important for gathering meteorological data.
questions.explanation: meteorological relates to weather science.

questions.content: 12. Fish use their fins for propulsion in the water.
questions.explanation: propulsion is the force that moves something forward.

questions.content: 13. I wish Dad wasn’t so innovative. He always comes into my room without knocking.
questions.explanation: innovative means thinking in creative ways, not entering without knocking.

questions.content: 14. Some metals are attracted to other metals due to an electromagnetic force.
questions.explanation: electromagnetic relates to electricity and magnetic fields.

questions.content: 15. Certain kinds of light can simulate flowers into producing seeds earlier than usual.
questions.explanation: should be stimulate, not simulate.

questions.content: 16. John is so ingenious. He hasn’t passed a single test so far this year.
questions.explanation: ingenious means smart, which contradicts not passing tests.

questions.content: 17. I’ve always been interested in meteors. That’s why I want to study meteorology.
questions.explanation: meteorology is weather, not meteors.

questions.content: 18. The lake was frightening. The water was still and dreary.
questions.explanation: dreary means dull, dark, lifeless.

questions.content: 19. Everyone who voted in the electron was given the day off of work.
questions.explanation: should be election, not electron.

questions.content: 20. The new pot looked perfect. It was covered in new, shiny defects.
questions.explanation: defects are flaws, so it wouldn't look perfect.

parts.title: Comprehensive Reading
parts.content:
The Tenacious Inventor

A young student of meteorology was having a difficult time with an experiment. He was attempting to duplicate lightning in clouds. He had made a device that could simulate lightning. It worked by releasing an electromagnetic pulse into the cloud. This pulse, in turn, stimulated the electrons in the cloud’s particles. Then the electrons produced lightning.

But his meteorological experiment had a major defect. He couldn’t get the device into the sky.

He had tied it to balloons, but they had burst. He had shot the device from a cannon, but the force of the cannon had damaged it.

“You should give up,” his friends told him. “You’ll never get that thing into the air.”

But his friends’ criticisms only spurred him to try again. The student was very innovative, and at last, he thought that he had an innovation that would work. He attached wings to the device, and on one dreary day, when clouds blocked the light of the sun, he started his experiment anew.

He placed the device on a rocket and launched it into the sky. The propulsion of the rocket carried the device high into the air. The rocket accelerated into the clouds and then released the device. It glided on its wings through the clouds, and when it penetrated the center of a large black cloud, it emitted the electromagnetic pulse. And just as he had predicted, lightning shot from the cloud!

He called his professors, and the next day they came to watch. He successfully duplicated the experiment. His teachers were extremely impressed and called the student and his invention ingenious.

The student was given many awards and became a famous inventor. He had not given up. He had remained tenacious and succeeded.

sections.title: Part A: Mark each statement T for true or F for false.

questions.content: 1. The student of meteorology had bought a device that simulated lightning in clouds.
questions.explanation: F, The student of meteorology had made a device that simulated lightning in clouds.

questions.content: 2. The electromagnetic pulse stimulated the electrons in the cloud’s particles.
questions.explanation: T

questions.content: 3. The student’s friends’ criticisms spurred him to try his experiment anew.
questions.explanation: T

questions.content: 4. It was a dreary day when the device glided into the clouds.
questions.explanation: T

questions.content: 5. The propulsion of the rocket accelerated the speed of the lightning.
questions.explanation: F, The propulsion of the rocket carried the device high into the air.

questions.content: 1. What was the defect of the student’s meteorological experiment?
options: It couldn't get into the sky.
questions.correctAnswer: It couldn't get into the sky.
questions.explanation: The meteorological experiment had a major defect. It couldn't get into the sky.

questions.content: 2. What innovation did the innovative student use to launch his device into the clouds?
options: He placed the device on a rocket and launched it into the sky.
He shot it from a cannon.
He carried it on a plane.
questions.correctAnswer: He placed the device on a rocket and launched it into the sky.
questions.explanation: He placed the device on a rocket and launched it into the sky.

questions.content: 3. For whom did the student duplicate his ingenious experiment?
questions.explanation: He duplicated the experiment for his professors.

questions.content: 4. What did the device do when it finally penetrated the center of a large black cloud?
questions.explanation: When it penetrated the center of a large black cloud, it emitted the electromagnetic pulse.

questions.content: 5. What happened to the student because he was tenacious?
options: He succeeded and became a famous inventor.
He gave up and studied something else.
questions.correctAnswer: He succeeded and became a famous inventor.
questions.explanation: Because he was so tenacious, the student had succeeded.
